summary: 1 finding checked (S-401): confirmed by execution plus a source read at head 77d2eff20. The card/record divergence is real; HUMAN_DECISION_PATTERN being an attribution check, not an identity proof, does not remove it (see evidence).

verifications.evidence: Command (run by the orchestrator, output in .metaproject/reviews/2026-10-19-review-flow-github-com-mrciphersmith-keryx-pull-1052-r05/research-evidence/verify-S-401-2.txt): bun <scratchpad>/verify-s401.ts, exit 0. Output: 'clip limit 300 stored length 360 shown length 301 / stored carries the attestation: human / operator-visible text carries it: none / stored tail not visible on card: true'. So a 360-char evidence that clip() cuts to 300 chars plus an ellipsis hides an 'operator: decided-by ...' tail that attestDismissal classifies as 'human' on the stored text and 'none' on what the operator saw. Source read at head 77d2eff20 backs the three sub-claims. (1) dispositionLine (operator-confirm-review.ts:692-693) is the only place the card shows evidence: the card lines at :769-777 are head, facts.evidence (the report's Evidence level line, not the dispositions), facts.waivers, dispositions.map(dispositionLine) and a static 'yes:' line; apply (:785-809) returns only a one-line 'review ... complete' output and shows nothing further. (2) The stored path is untruncated: completionDispositions (:687) stores evidence.trim(); the same prepared.dispositions array goes to completeReviewGated (runCompletionGates :822-823) where recordDispositionsLocked (managed.ts:1958-1959) writes record.evidence verbatim into findings.json, and to writeCompletionRecord (:806) for completion-confirmation.json. No length cap or entry-count cap exists in completionDispositions or in the schema. (3) After recordDispositions, managed.ts:1056-1057 re-reads findings.json and calls writeReviewNotes, which calls attestDismissal (review-notes.ts:308) on the stored evidence; HUMAN_DECISION_PATTERN (:122) matches and a note is written for a dismissed-incorrect finding. The shell-bridge.ts:275-279 guard (operatorCardTooLongForTopic) does not cover this: it only measures the whole card against MAX_APPROVAL_PROMPT_CHARS, and a line clipped to 301 chars never trips it, so the card still gets Yes/No buttons. Weighing the attribution caveat: review-notes.ts:111-121 says the pattern is an attribution requirement, not an identity proof, and that is true, but the finding's stated defect is not forgeable identity; it is that the text the operator confirmed differs from the text recorded and acted on. That divergence is real and the caveat does not touch it. What the caveat does change is the consequence: the harm is limited to a learning note being filed on an unread attestation, and an agent could already write 'human: alice' in the first 300 characters, where the operator would at least see it. Not a refutation. Also noted, for the orchestrator to weigh rather than for this verdict: clip() appends an ellipsis, so the card does signal elision, and the same clip is used for waiver quotes (:708, :719, :723), so the pattern predates dispositions; that does not make the operator able to read the hidden part.
